_comment: The most period-legible garment in the menu. A stripe down the sleeve and an elasticated cuff date a frame on their own, without a single word about how the picture looks. Note what is NOT here: no weather, no place, no time of day. climate below is the machine-readable channel for all of that, and checkCompatibility reads it -- the prose must not. REWRITTEN 2026-08-27 twice, and the second rewrite is the interesting one. First pass: zipped rather than hanging open, matching pants stated, chest crest deleted -- all four landed on the first render (20260827-154405-73ca3d). STRIPES took three renders to settle and never obeyed. The line asked for two, then for 'exactly two' with the pair named again on the leg and two negatives aimed at three; seedream drew THREE every time (20260824-114051-4209a6, 20260827-154405-73ca3d, 20260827-160513-cbb476). Three stripes on a navy tracksuit is adidas's registered trade dress, and 'large brand logo' never caught it because it is not a logo applied to the garment -- it IS the garment. THE PATTERN WORTH KEEPING: this model honours PRESENCE and ignores COUNT. Every add-or-remove instruction landed first time; the one numeric instruction was overridden three times out of three on both the positive and negative channels. So the garment lost its number instead: ONE broad stripe is a thing to draw or not draw. CONFIRMED on 20260827-161556-cfe684: one broad stripe, drawn as one, on both sleeve and leg, counted on a 2.4x crop. Four renders and $0.16 settled this. Do not 'restore' two stripes here -- it has been tried three times, it costs $0.04 a go, and it does not work. test/catalog.test.js pins the absence of a count.
label: Tracksuit
wardrobe: a full-zip tracksuit jacket in navy with a single broad white stripe running down the outside of each sleeve, a stand collar zipped to the throat, elasticated cuffs and hem, and matching navy track pants with a single broad white stripe down the outside leg, worn over a plain white t-shirt
negatives: multiple parallel stripes down the arm or leg
